senses.gloss: , Poël סוֹבַר (Saf. of ברי; cmp. Arab. sabar exploravit vulnus &c., misbâr specillum vulnerarium) to perforate, cut, (only used in the sense of) to let blood. Part. pass. מְסוֹבַר.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 112a:1">Pes. 112ᵃ</cite> top <he>דמס׳ ולא משי וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>מְסוֹכַר</he>, v. <cite ref="O00942"><he>סְכַר</he> II</cite>) he who has been bled and has not washed his hands.
<cite ref="Yevamot 72a:4">Yeb. 72ᵃ</cite> <he>לא מְסוֹבְרִינָן ביה</he> Ar. (ed. <he>מסוכ׳</he>) and on it (that day) we must not be bled.
<cite ref="Meilah 20b">Meïl. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>דמס׳ ואכל וכ׳</he> (ed. <he>דמסוכ׳</he>; Ar. <he>דסַבַּר</he>, prob. clerical error, v. Koh. Ar. Compl. s. v.) he who eats fowl after blood-letting.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 28b:13">Ab. Zar. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>דכאיב ליה עינא ודמ׳</he> Ag. Hatt. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 7) one having pain of the eye and one who has been bled.—V. <he>סִיבּוּרָא</he> II.
